news.headline: NeurAxis Reports Record Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Driven by 116% Year Over Year Revenue Growth
news.summary: NeurAxis posted Q2 2026 revenue of $1.93 million, up 116% year over year, its eighth straight quarter of double-digit growth, driven by the new Category I CPT code for PENFS that took effect January 1, 2026. Gross margin expanded to 85.9% and average selling price rose 28% to $992 per device as more sales moved to full reimbursement, though cash on hand was $8.3 million with continued reliance on ATM and warrant financing.

news.headline: NeurAxis Falls on Q2 2026 EPS Miss Despite 116% Revenue Growth
news.summary: Shares fell roughly 7% to about $6.40 after NeurAxis reported a wider-than-expected Q2 loss of $0.19 per share versus a forecast $0.16 loss, even as revenue growth beat expectations. Management flagged higher expected cash burn in the second half of 2026 as it invests in new commercial hires ahead of larger payer wins.

news.headline: NeurAxis Expands Payer Coverage with New Policies
news.summary: NeurAxis announced additional regional medical policy coverage for PENFS in the Mid-Atlantic region, extending reimbursement access to over 500,000 covered lives. CEO Brian Carrico said the company continues building toward comprehensive nationwide written policy coverage for IB-Stim.

news.headline: NeurAxis to Host Second Quarter 2026 Results and Business Update Call on Tuesday, August 11, 2026
news.summary: NeurAxis announced it would report Q2 2026 financial results before market open on August 11, 2026, followed by a conference call and business update at 9:00 am ET the same day.

news.headline: NeurAxis Declares Q2 2026 Stock Dividend on Series B Preferred Stock
news.summary: NeurAxis's board declared its Q2 2026 Series B Preferred dividend, payable entirely in about 80,463 shares of common stock rather than cash, based on the 8.5% annual cumulative dividend rate. The dividend was paid July 29, 2026 to holders of record as of July 21, 2026, conserving company cash at the cost of modest additional dilution.

news.headline: NeurAxis (NRXS) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
news.summary: On the earnings call, management said three new commercial hires made in Q2 were already showing results and that several more hires are planned for Q3 as part of a strategy to saturate the six-to-eight states with strong payer coverage. Executives reiterated they expect to add larger payers in the second half of 2026 into 2027, which they said would improve the company's going-concern outlook.

catalysts.label: Additional large national payer coverage decisions
catalysts.detail: Management said it expects to sign one or more larger national payers for PENFS/IB-Stim reimbursement in the second half of 2026 into 2027, which it expects to materially improve revenue and its going-concern position.

catalysts.label: Expanded commercial sales team
catalysts.detail: NeurAxis plans additional commercial/field sales hires in Q3 2026 to deepen penetration in states with existing payer coverage, following three new hires added in Q2.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings report
catalysts.detail: NeurAxis is expected to report third-quarter 2026 financial results and host its next quarterly business update call, consistent with its recent quarterly reporting cadence.

catalysts.label: Continued PENFS payer policy expansion
catalysts.detail: The company is pursuing further regional and national medical policy coverage wins for PENFS beyond the 500,000 covered lives added in early August 2026, building toward comprehensive nationwide reimbursement.

catalysts.label: VA Federal Supply Schedule ramp
catalysts.detail: Following its December 2025 VA Federal Supply Schedule contract award, NeurAxis is working to ramp IB-Stim sales into the Veterans Affairs health system, which serves roughly 7 million patients annually.

pulse: NeurAxis just posted a record Q2 2026 (revenue up 116% YoY to $1.93M, gross margin near 86%) as the new Category I CPT code for PENFS drives higher reimbursement, but shares sold off after the report on a wider-than-expected per-share loss and management's warning of higher cash burn in the second half of 2026. The company remains a going-concern-flagged microcap ($8.3M cash as of June 30) that continues to fund operations via its ATM facility and preferred-stock dividends paid in stock rather than cash, while it expands payer coverage (500,000+ newly covered lives in the Mid-Atlantic in early August) and grows its commercial sales team. The near-term thesis hinges on landing larger national payers in H2 2026/2027 to reach cash-flow breakeven before capital needs bite further.
